description: Orbital provides the gamified way of experimenting gravity of different planets/satellites.
summary:
Orbital Gravity is an interactive 3D space exploration game that allows users to experience how gravity differs across planets and moons in our solar system.

Built with Next.js, React Three Fiber, and Three.js, the project features five explorable environments: Earth, the Moon, Mars, Europa, and Titan. Players control an astronaut, navigate planetary surfaces, and experiment with jumping under different gravitational conditions.

Each destination applies its own surface gravity, allowing users to observe how the same jumping force produces different heights and airtimes. By turning gravitational acceleration into an interactive experience, Orbital Gravity makes abstract physics concepts more intuitive and engaging.

The project addresses the challenge of making space science accessible through hands-on learning rather than passive observation. It combines interactive simulation, game design, and planetary exploration to encourage curiosity about physics, space environments, and future exploration beyond Earth.

Overview

Orbital Gravity is a browser-based 3D space science simulator that makes planetary gravity, meteor collisions, and physics education interactive and accessible.

Players can explore five planetary environments—Earth, Moon, Mars, Europa, and Titan—each featuring distinct scenery and gravity-dependent astronaut movement.

The project combines NASA data, interactive meteor impact experiments, AI-powered science education, and Solana NFT collectibles.

How It Works

1. Planetary Gravity Exploration

Players control an astronaut using WASD or arrow keys and jump using the spacebar. Each planetary environment applies its corresponding gravitational acceleration.

The simulation uses three fundamental physics equations:

  • Vertical velocity: \(v=v_0-gt\)
  • Vertical position: \(y=y_0+v_0t-\frac12gt^2\)
  • Maximum jump height: \(h=\frac{v_0^2}{2g}\)

By maintaining a consistent initial jumping velocity, players can compare jump height and airtime across different planetary environments.

2. Meteor Impact Lab

Meteor Lab allows players to experiment with meteor collisions by adjusting meteoroid diameter, impact velocity, impact angle, and planetary destination.

The default experiment simulates a 2-meter meteoroid impacting the Moon at 20 km/s and a 45-degree angle.

The simulator calculates kinetic energy using:

\[ E_k=\frac12mv^2 \]

Players can visualize the meteor's trajectory, collision, impact flash, and surface effects in a 3D environment.

The project integrates NASA/JPL Fireball Data API records to connect simulated experiments with real-world observations of meteoroids entering Earth's atmosphere.

The simulation is educational and uses simplified impact physics rather than a fully validated crater prediction model.

3. Orbit AI — Science Chat Assistant

Orbital Gravity includes an AI-powered science assistant that allows players to ask questions while exploring planetary environments.

Example questions include:

  • What happens when a meteor hits the Moon?
  • Why do meteors burn up in Earth's atmosphere?
  • How does gravity affect meteor collisions?
  • Why are impact craters preserved on the Moon?

Orbit AI integrates Vultr AI Inference and Google Gemini through a server-side Next.js API.

The application supports automatic provider fallback to maintain access to AI-powered science explanations.

4. Solana NFT Collectibles

Players can capture screenshots of their planetary exploration and meteor impact experiments.

The application integrates Phantom Wallet, Solana Devnet, Metaplex, and Pinata IPFS to support minting screenshots as blockchain collectibles.

The NFT workflow consists of capturing an image, uploading it to IPFS, creating NFT metadata, minting on Solana Devnet, and displaying a Solana Explorer link.

NASA/JPL Fireball Data API

https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/doc/fireball.html

NASA Planetary Fact Sheet

https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/

Provides planetary physical properties used as scientific references for gravity-based exploration.

Best Use of Solana

Orbital Gravity integrates Solana blockchain technology to turn interactive space science experiments into digital collectibles.

Players can capture screenshots of planetary exploration and meteor impact simulations and mint them as NFTs on Solana Devnet.

Using Phantom Wallet, Metaplex, and Pinata IPFS, the application connects STEM education with blockchain ownership and shareable exploration experiences.

Best Use of Vultr

Orbital Gravity integrates Vultr AI Inference as the primary AI service for Orbit AI, an interactive educational assistant embedded in the game.

The assistant helps players understand meteor collisions, impact energy, planetary gravity, and crater formation through natural-language conversations.

The backend uses Vultr's chat completions API and supports automatic fallback to Gemini, demonstrating a flexible AI architecture for interactive science education.

Best Use of Gemini

Orbital Gravity integrates Google Gemini to provide conversational science explanations within the 3D simulation.

Players can ask questions about meteor impacts, gravity, planetary atmospheres, and NASA observations while conducting experiments.

Gemini receives experiment context, including the selected planet and meteor parameters, enabling explanations connected to the player's simulation.

The integration makes complex physics concepts easier to understand through interactive, AI-assisted learning.

Best Use of GoDaddy

Orbital Gravity is designed as a publicly accessible educational web application that allows students and space enthusiasts to explore planetary science without installing software.

Creativity and Innovation

Orbital Gravity combines four technologies into a unified educational experience: interactive 3D physics simulation, NASA observational data, conversational AI, and blockchain collectibles.

Instead of learning gravity solely through equations, players experience different gravitational environments, conduct meteor impact experiments, ask AI questions, and preserve their exploration experiences as digital collectibles.

Intended Impact

Orbital Gravity aims to make space science more engaging and accessible for students, educators, and space enthusiasts.

Its long-term vision is to become an interactive STEM learning platform featuring additional NASA datasets, planetary challenges, realistic impact models, educational missions, and AI-guided experiments.

Design Considerations

The application prioritizes browser accessibility, intuitive controls, scientifically grounded reference data, and interactive learning.

Physics calculations are simplified for educational purposes. Meteor impact visuals do not represent scientifically validated crater predictions, and NASA Earth fireball observations are distinguished from hypothetical impacts on other worlds.
